title: Six of 42 ozone survival records measured dispersal in a 2024 invertebrate data release
abstract: We checked endpoint meaning in the ozone survival category of a 2024 invertebrate data release. Six of 42 records measured alarm-response dispersal. Two more had dead-aphid labels. The remaining 34 records from nine papers measured survival or emergence. Their equal-paper mean stored log ratio was -0.0673. Single-paper omission gave means from -0.1564 to +0.0250. A strict survival-label rule gave -0.1554 from six papers. These are descriptive summaries, not survival probabilities or population effect estimates. Only one of the nine survival-or-emergence papers was published after 2004. Region and publication-era cells had seven, one, one and zero papers. The selected data cannot support the planned repeated test across two regions and two eras. Endpoint labels, shared experiments, source orientation of means and paper selection limit inference. We do not repeat the original meta-analysis or test climate interactions. Code, aggregate results, source provenance, a figure and independent numerical checks are included. External source records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Endpoint definitions change equal-paper summaries. Lines show single-paper omission ranges, not confidence intervals. The support grid counts papers with survival or emergence outcomes. Publication era is not observation period.
